title: 9th Circuit Rejects Trump Administration's Expansion of Mandatory Migrant Detention
detail: The San Francisco-based 9th US Circuit Court of Appeals ruled 2-1 on July 30, 2026 that the Trump administration cannot deny immigrants detained inside the United States a chance at bond hearings, rejecting the administration's expansion of mandatory detention to cover anyone who ever crossed the border illegally — even those who have lived in the US for years. A judge appointed by Trump joined the majority. The ruling is the fourth of six appeals-court decisions to go against the policy (two have sided with the administration), and follows a similar 5th Circuit ruling on July 2 requiring bond hearings within 90 days. The Supreme Court is expected to eventually take up the issue.

media.caption: 9th Circuit rules against Trump administration's mandatory migrant detention expansion
